program.welcome: Boys and girls of every skill level are welcome
about: We're a volunteer-run youth soccer club. Players learn to dribble, pass, and shoot, and they learn to play as a team.
Younger players play small-sided games so everyone touches the ball a lot. Every player gets real playing time.

pillars.title: Touch the Ball
pillars.text: Small-sided games mean more touches and more fun.

pillars.title: Everyone Plays
pillars.text: Fair playing time for every player, every game.

pillars.title: Respect the Game
pillars.text: Respect for teammates, opponents, coaches, and referees.

pillars.title: Have Fun
pillars.text: Kids who love the game keep playing it.

groups.name: U6
groups.text: 3v3 or 4v4 games with no goalkeepers. Lots of touches and lots of fun.

groups.name: U8
groups.text: 4v4 games and the first simple rules: throw-ins, kickoffs, and teamwork.

groups.name: U10
groups.text: 7v7 games with goalkeepers, passing, and positions.

groups_intro: Teams are grouped by birth year ("U8" means under 8), so players compete with kids their own age.

join_steps.title: Ask Us
join_steps.text: Email us with your child's age and any questions. We'll tell you which team fits.

join_steps.title: Try a Practice
join_steps.text: Come watch or join a practice. No commitment, no cost.

join_steps.title: Register
join_steps.text: Fill out the registration, medical, and permission forms before the season starts, and you're on the team.

uniform: We provide a jersey. Players need shin guards (required at every practice and game), soccer socks to cover them, cleats or athletic shoes, a size-appropriate ball, and a full water bottle.

safety.title: Player Safety
points: Every coach and volunteer completes abuse-prevention training and a background check before working with players.
Two adults are present at every practice and game. No adult is ever alone with a player who isn't their own child.

Coaches learn the signs of a concussion. Any player with a suspected head injury sits out until a health care provider clears them. Heading the ball isn't part of practice or games for our youngest players.
We post photos of players only with written permission from a parent or guardian, and never with a player's full name.

faq.a: No. We teach the basics, and every player gets playing time.

faq.q: When and where do you practice and play?

faq.a: Shin guards, socks that cover them, cleats or athletic shoes, a ball (size 3 for U8 and under, size 4 through U12, size 5 after that), and a water bottle.
Every team needs a few helpers: coaches, team parents, snack and field volunteers. No experience needed, and we'll train you.

faq.q: What happens when the weather is bad?
faq.a: Safety comes first. We stop for lightning and extreme heat, and we email families as soon as a practice or game is canceled.

faq.q: Can we try it before signing up?
faq.a: Yes! Email {email} and we'll invite you to a practice.
